blockers.quote: The teacher's chance of finishing the syllabus: three per cent. The loud boy: zero. The topper's real dream is music: nought point two. The chaiwala's café: sixty-one.
blockers.why: Story #5 fails: this is an "and then" montage of readings, not a causal turn.
blockers.fix: Replace with: "You check the teacher expecting certainty; three per cent. Therefore you trust the topper—but her chip names music, not the exam. So you test the chaiwala, expecting another fantasy; sixty-one. You abandon the exam for the safest-looking target."

blockers.quote: each use has a gap: the topper is not who you thought
blockers.why: Story #6 fails: only the topper supplies an expectation/result gap; the teacher, loud boy and chaiwala are merely listed.
blockers.fix: Give every retained reading an explicit expectation and surprise, as in the teacher/topper/chaiwala sequence above; cut the loud boy unless his result also reverses a stated expectation.

blockers.quote: The fact lands on you: seats against applicants for one exam, one number at a time
blockers.why: Story #7 fails: the outline asserts that the fact lands but gives no action or consequence within two lines, and the ratio does not yet explain why the belief failed.
blockers.fix: Replace with: "You take the fat-number placement and stop studying; therefore your mock score and chip fall. At forty-eight per cent, one sourced comparison reveals that seats per applicant is a crowd base rate, not an individual verdict. Within the next line, you reopen your notes and the chip responds."

blockers.quote: cousin named in the first minute, warm beats: he bowls to you in the lane
blockers.why: Story #9 fails: no earlier beat actually names or shows the cousin, so the outline has not earned his loss two minutes in advance; his recovery is also disconnected from the climactic choice.
blockers.fix: Add an explicit beat near 0:45 where he bowls to you, you adjust his grip and promise another game. At the 75–80% choice, make obeying the safe number mean leaving his bat hidden; you return it and let him choose before choosing your own exam.

blockers.quote: The turn breaks "A number can't lie to you": it didn't lie
blockers.why: Story #10 fails: "it didn't lie" confirms the planted line instead of contradicting it.
blockers.fix: Change the early plant to "The biggest number is the right choice." Break it here with: "The biggest number can tell you what is likely. It cannot tell you what is worth choosing."

blockers.quote: it described the crowd and you were never the crowd
blockers.why: The no-new-power-rule-after-halfway check fails: this first redefines personal chips as crowd statistics after 65%.
blockers.fix: State by 0:30 that chips begin with a crowd base rate and update from what each person currently does. Make the late turn about mistaking likelihood for value, not a newly revealed chip mechanism.

blockers.quote: one sourced long shot that worked among them
blockers.why: The no-new-person-after-60% check fails if this late example introduces a successful person after 65%.
blockers.fix: Cut the new example and build the city image from already planted people—the teacher, topper, chaiwala and cousin.

suggestions.fix: Make the year visible through three escalating actions—a missed mock test, accepting the safe placement and hiding the bat—rather than spending this section explaining the rule.

suggestions.quote: his chip falls to zero the moment he nods
suggestions.fix: Make this the moving wordless peak: hold eight seconds while the counter drains, his hand leaves the bat and it rolls out of frame.

suggestions.quote: What counts as success, who decides?
suggestions.fix: Answer during the rule beat: the chip follows the goal that person would choose with nobody watching.

suggestions.quote: Does it know my effort? Does it change if I study harder?
suggestions.fix: Before 35%, show one experiment: you study expecting an instant rise; nothing changes until the next mock result, when the chip moves.

suggestions.quote: What does 0.04% even mean in people?
suggestions.fix: At the initial reveal, turn the hall into one lit chair among two thousand five hundred, then return immediately to your face.
